cards.front: light source
cards.back: An object that gives out its own light. The Sun, a lamp and a candle flame are light sources.
cards.say: light source. An object that gives out its own light. The Sun, a lamp and a candle flame are light sources.

cards.front: Is the Moon a light source?
cards.back: No. It does not make light. It reflects light from the Sun.
cards.say: Is the Moon a light source? No. It does not make light. It reflects light from the Sun.

cards.front: How does light travel?
cards.back: In straight lines.
cards.say: How does light travel? In straight lines.

cards.front: opaque
cards.back: Does not let any light through. Wood and metal are opaque.
cards.say: opaque. Does not let any light through. Wood and metal are opaque.

cards.front: transparent
cards.back: Lets light through so you can see clearly through it. Clear glass is transparent.
cards.say: transparent. Lets light through so you can see clearly through it. Clear glass is transparent.

cards.front: translucent
cards.back: Lets some light through, but you cannot see clearly through it. Frosted glass is translucent.
cards.say: translucent. Lets some light through, but you cannot see clearly through it. Frosted glass is translucent.

cards.front: shadow
cards.back: A dark area made when an opaque object blocks light.
cards.say: shadow. A dark area made when an opaque object blocks light.

cards.front: Why does a shadow form?
cards.back: Light travels in straight lines and an opaque object blocks it, so no light reaches the area behind.
cards.say: Why does a shadow form? Light travels in straight lines and an opaque object blocks it, so no light reaches the area behind.

cards.front: What does a shadow show about an object?
cards.back: Its shape, as a dark outline. It is black or dark grey and shows no colour or detail.
cards.say: What does a shadow show about an object? Its shape, as a dark outline. It is black or dark grey and shows no colour or detail.

cards.front: What happens to a shadow when the object moves closer to the light source?
cards.back: The shadow gets bigger.
cards.say: What happens to a shadow when the object moves closer to the light source? The shadow gets bigger.

cards.front: What happens to a shadow when the object moves further from the light source?
cards.back: The shadow gets smaller.
cards.say: What happens to a shadow when the object moves further from the light source? The shadow gets smaller.

cards.front: When is your shadow longest in the day?
cards.back: Early morning and late afternoon, when the Sun is low in the sky.
cards.say: When is your shadow longest in the day? Early morning and late afternoon, when the Sun is low in the sky.

cards.front: When is your shadow shortest in the day?
cards.back: Around midday, when the Sun is highest in the sky.
cards.say: When is your shadow shortest in the day? Around midday, when the Sun is highest in the sky.

cards.front: Why does a shadow change length during the day?
cards.back: The Sun seems to move across the sky, and the height of the Sun changes the length of shadows.
cards.say: Why does a shadow change length during the day? The Sun seems to move across the sky, and the height of the Sun changes the length of shadows.

cards.front: sundial
cards.back: A tool that tells the time. The shadow of a pointer moves around a dial as the Sun seems to move.
cards.say: sundial. A tool that tells the time. The shadow of a pointer moves around a dial as the Sun seems to move.

cards.front: How long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth?
cards.back: About eight minutes.
cards.say: How long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth? About eight minutes.

cards.front: Which makes the darkest shadow: opaque, translucent or transparent?
cards.back: Opaque. It blocks all the light.
cards.say: Which makes the darkest shadow: opaque, translucent or transparent? Opaque. It blocks all the light.

cards.front: Can you see a shadow in a completely dark room?
cards.back: No. You need a light source to make a shadow.
cards.say: Can you see a shadow in a completely dark room? No. You need a light source to make a shadow.

cards.front: ray
cards.back: A straight line with an arrow that shows the path of light.
cards.say: ray. A straight line with an arrow that shows the path of light.

cards.front: How do you make a shadow puppet?
cards.back: Hold the puppet between a light source and a screen. The puppet blocks the light.
cards.say: How do you make a shadow puppet? Hold the puppet between a light source and a screen. The puppet blocks the light.

cards.front: Why do we have night time?
cards.back: Earth spins. The side facing away from the Sun is in Earth's shadow.
cards.say: Why do we have night time? Earth spins. The side facing away from the Sun is in Earth's shadow.

cards.front: Does the Sun move across the sky?
cards.back: It seems to, but it is Earth that spins, so the Sun only seems to move.
cards.say: Does the Sun move across the sky? It seems to, but it is Earth that spins, so the Sun only seems to move.
